message.content: {"caption":"A four-stage WikiSkill workflow links three knowledge layers through trace analysis, skill updates, validation, and iterative feedback.","description":"A flow diagram has three wide, rounded gray layers stacked above a row of four colored process boxes. From top to bottom: the Skill Layer (skills/) contains “Evolving Procedural Knowledge” and is marked “Reversible, Conditional Update”; a folder icon represents the stored skills. The Wiki Layer (wiki/) contains “Structured Patterns & Evolution Logs” and is marked “Compounding, Never Reset”; a lit-bulb-and-books icon represents organized knowledge. The Raw Layer (raw/) contains “Immutable Execution Traces” and is marked “Permanent, Write Once”; a lock icon represents protected, immutable traces. The four stages run left to right: Step 1, “Inference Agent,” executes rollouts on the Training Set; a robot icon represents the agent. Step 2, “Wiki Maintainer,” performs root-cause analysis on traces; a tool/gears icon represents maintenance and analysis. Step 3, “Skill Proposer,” proposes skill updates from Wiki and Traces; a lit bulb represents proposing ideas. Step 4, “Gating & Rollback,” evaluates the skill candidate on the Validation Set; its icon shows a checked box and an X, representing the gate’s accept/reject or rollback decisions. Horizontal arrows connect Step 1 to Step 2 (blue), Step 2 to Step 3 (red), and Step 3 to Step 4 (yellow). Between the layers and the stages, a blue arrow labeled “Inject Skills” points down into Step 1, while a blue arrow labeled “Write Traces” points up from Step 1 to the Raw Layer. A red arrow labeled “Sample Traces” points down from the Raw Layer to Step 2, and a red arrow labeled “Consolidate Patterns” points up from Step 2 to the Wiki Layer. Three yellow arrows point down into Step 3 from the Skill, Wiki, and Raw layers; their label is “Read Skill, Wiki, Traces.” From Step 4, a green upward arrow labeled “Update the Skill if Better” leads to the Skill Layer, and another green upward arrow labeled “Update Wiki Logs” leads to the Wiki Layer. A green return path labeled “Next Iteration” runs from Step 4 beneath the stages and points upward into Step 1. Short unlabeled blue vertical connector segments also appear between the stacked layers at the left.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
